subject: Culture
title: Gift Wrapping Codes
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Gift Wrapping Codes.

hook.text: In Japan, white wrapping paper is for funerals. Use it for a birthday gift and you've wished someone dead.

buildup.text: Gift wrapping signals intent before the box is opened. Color, material, and technique all carry meaning.

discovery.text: Japanese 'furoshiki' cloth wrapping is an art form—each fold pattern communicates a different message.

twist.text: In Korea, wrapping matters as much as content. A poorly wrapped expensive gift is worse than a well-wrapped cheap one.

climax.text: Western cultures wrap to create surprise. Asian cultures wrap to show respect. Same act, different goals.

punchline.text: The wrapping is the first message, before the gift speaks.

quiz.question: What is the Japanese art of cloth gift wrapping called?
